suggestions.assertion: Gives a locator-strategy distribution with real counts/percentages (not just an impression), roughly matching the ~31%/31%/38% positional/id/css split
suggestions.reason: The manifest's split is scoped to the 55 page-object field declarations, but a reasonable review also counts the 27 inline test locators and uses a by-selector-type taxonomy, which gives 44/29/14/13 or 25/31/44. 'Roughly matching' is underspecified. Accept either scope and grade on whether the counts are grep-correct for the scope the run states.

suggestions.assertion: Reports a quantified count of assertion-free test methods (expects 4, e.g. in ProductGridTests.java and InvoiceLookupTests.java)
suggestions.reason: The fixture has 2 more assertion-free @Test methods in the wip package, which testng.xml runs, so 6 is equally correct. Update the expectation to '4 (or 6 if wip tests are counted)'.

suggestions.assertion: Reports a quantified empty-catch-block / swallowed-exception count...
suggestions.reason: The manifest's 37 excludes BasePage.dismissCookieBanner, whose catch body holds only a comment. A structural count gives 38. The manifest should state its definition (comment-only bodies counted or not) so graders don't flag correct runs.

Both runs found significant real defects the manifest omits: javax.mail compile failure, IRetryAnalyzer miswired as a listener, config.properties never read, step comments promising checks that are never made, vacuous assertNotNull(getText()) assertions, and production DB targeting. Consider adding them to the manifest so future runs that miss them are caught.

No assertion checks for false positives or invented evidence (e.g. a wrong file:line or an inflated count). A spot-check assertion, such as '3 randomly chosen file:line citations resolve to the described code', would discriminate between careful and sloppy reviews.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions mostly discriminate well: the format assertions (tags, FIRST, exact checklist columns) clearly separate skill from baseline. Several count-based expectations are stricter than the fixture's ground truth warrants (wip tests, comment-only catches, locator scope).
